findings.reason: a node sent to runs.py for the discard result finds no such surface and must either edit the wrong module or add a second discard result beside the real one in promotion.py, the exact duplication the section's reuse stance forbids.
findings.text: §5 says "the discard result in `reckon/crew/runs.py` reads the stacking recorded on the holder's pointer and name[s] each descendant still live", but `reckon/crew/runs.py` defines no discard: `discard(run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]`, which is the discard result, is at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:1832`, and the string "discard" appears in runs.py only inside two comments (reckon/crew/runs.py:604, reckon/crew/runs.py:1454)

findings.reason: the only revision a node finds on the pointer is `base_sha`, so compiling the equality against it admits a dispatch based beneath the holder's tip, which carries none of the holder's 38 unlanded commits — the opposite of the exception's purpose — and the guard would then pass a case it was written to refuse.
findings.text: §5 requires "the dispatch's base is the holder's head" and says each `_RepositoryScopeClaim` carries "its head revision and whether its process has stopped as fields, read from `claim_disposition`, whose `ClaimDisposition` gains a `stopped` flag beside `binding`", but `ClaimDisposition` gains only the `stopped` flag (reckon/crew/node.py:1487-1497) and the live pointer records `base_sha` — the holder's own dispatch base — and never a head (reckon/crew/node.py:1465); the holder's head is only obtainable by reading its worktree, as `unintegrated_claim_work` does (`rev-list HEAD ^integration_ref ^base_sha`, reckon/crew/node.py:1467-1469) or via `_head_revision` (reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:1814). The same gap leaves the ancestry test unspecified: the pass condition is stated as an equality ("the dispatch's base is the holder's head"), yet the mechanism names `_revision_is_ancestor` / `_is_ancestor` without stating which two revisions must stand in that relation

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §5 cites the discard result at `reckon/crew/runs.py`, where no discard function exists.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's done-when is falsifiable and carries a control: the fixture dispatch based on main is refused `ScopeConflict`, and on the base commit the stacked dispatch is refused, so the test fails there.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5's measure is an in-repo fixture test and it names no scratch or node-local path; §6's evidence is the pass JSON on stdout plus `admission-verdicts.jsonl`, a durable run-store path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 and §6 introduce no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into symbols or comments; the run ids and revisions in §5's Why are the plan document's own evidence.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5 names the holder's head revision as a fact the claim carries but names no source for it, and the only revision on the holder's live pointer is its dispatch base.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one deliverable, the base-conditional exception, with its recording and result-naming as the same mechanism's consequences rather than a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan's only declared relationship, `plan-after` → `work-is-checked-against-its-domain#s2`, resolves to a §2 that exists in that plan, and the nodes §5 and §6 name write disjoint files as `f-accd-002` states.
